lenses.verification_red_team: C1 core facts (Culkin as Kevin, 47 markets, W+K Toronto, socks, Little Nero's fries, 'Leave adulthood behind', US Dec 1) confirmed across the official release + 3 independent outlets. Launch date conflicts (Ads of the World credits Nov 16; Adweek/DesignRush Nov 17): say 'this week' / 'mid-November'. No view or sales numbers exist in sources: do not claim 'viral' numerically; say 'everyone's talking' only as coverage-based estimate. The '7 weeks after vowing own IP' claim (C1b) is a paraphrase with a contradicting Adweek framing: keep off screen. Do not say the meal is available everywhere: US Dec 1, markets vary. Do not claim Culkin's fee or Disney deal terms. Age 46 is computed from his 1980 birth year (public fact) - safe to say 'now in his forties' if unsure.
lenses.audience_psychology: Home Alone is a shared childhood ritual for both audiences (Persian viewers grew up with it on TV, an estimate). The hook is self-recognition: 'this ad is about you, not your kids'. Curiosity gap: why would a fast-food giant aim its biggest Christmas ad at 40-year-olds? Shareable: people send nostalgia to siblings/friends. Risk: nostalgia topics can feel soft; keep the strategic edge (who the real customer is, what is being sold).
lenses.brand_fit: Fits brand strategy/positioning pillar: selling a feeling and a former self, not a product; adults as the new Happy Meal customer (kidult pattern: McDonaldland adult meal 2025, Minecraft meal 'for adults'). Practical lesson for business owners: find the memory your customer already owns and give them a way to step back into it, with a collectible (socks) as the souvenir. Not political, no private individuals.
